decisions.reason: After four years and two years without website visibility, this adjustable quarter-pallet display likely has revealed limited standalone demand relative to several similar core products, so its option value is mostly spent.

The pegboard-back variant still fits core capabilities, but by 2022 the market test should largely be complete and the lack of continued prominence suggests too little value to keep another overlapping option open.
As a fairly standard quarter-pallet concept that overlaps with other cardboard display formats, it is now more likely to be rationalized out of a narrow portfolio than kept as an unresolved option.

The eighth-pallet format is a distinct and low-cost extension of the firm's core display range, so management would still be inclined to retain it as a viable standard option despite limited recent visibility.
Because the wooden display pallet is farther from the firm's paper-based core and has not remained visibly marketed, its remaining upside no longer justifies continued support.
Its niche media focus and overlap with other quarter-pallet displays mean uncertainty should be largely resolved by now, making abandonment the more likely choice.
